newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend profit-taking, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend profit-taking, seen falling.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the third session running on Monday and analysts saw the market extending its profit-taking correction after it rose 30 percent since the beginning of the year.

The main market's WIG index fell 124.1 points, or 0.7 percent, to 17,419.7, and turnover eased 2.9 percent to 188.8 million zlotys ($60.9 million) on all three markets as 60 issues fell, 18 rose and 11 were flat.
"The market is reacting to recent growth...and one can expect the falls, which started last week to be continued," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.

Some analysts said the market was likely to fall to 17,000 points of the WIG index before stabilising or rebounding but others saw only 16,000 or 16,500, the late January level, when the latest wave of growth began, providing strong support.
Some analysts said the correction was likely to last one or two weeks, but others said it could extend to the next three weeks, with possible phases of stabilisation or limited growth.
Some said most construction firms, recent bargains, seemed already fairly priced, after their gains since early January elevated their P/Es to about 20 against the market average of 16.2.
They said textile firms seemed cheap as they traded at less than 10 times their earnings, but said the whole sector's rather gloomy prospects were discouraging investors.
Polish road builder Gdanskie Przedsiebiorstwo Robot Drogowych SA (GPRD) started main market trade at 16.7 zlotys ($5.4), 49 percent above its issue price.
Continuous trade turover amounted to 7.4 million zlotys ($2.4 million) with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,750.1 points, 0.7 percent lower than at the regular session.
